To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) income segmentation matters, and (2) income mobility outcomes are not random
Households in the Philippines are segmented according to income, but the income segments are not permanent.
(1) the propensity to move up or down the income distribution is not equal for all income segments, and (2) the income segmentation that matters is initial income.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether the income distribution of the Philippines is more or less stable over time, and if not, how much income mobility there is and whether the poor have a better chance of improving their income status than the rich.
the extent to which income segmentation affects the income mobility prospects of Filipinos.
the relationship between income segmentation and income mobility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
income segmentation based on initial income is a more useful tool than permanent income in assessing income mobility in the Philippines.
income segmentation affects income mobility, and that the effect is more pronounced when income segmentation is based on initial income rather than permanent income.
initial income segmentation is a better predictor of future income mobility than permanent income segmentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
income segmentation matters for income mobility outcomes.
while the poor in the Philippines are less likely to remain poor in the future, their chances of escaping poverty are also lower than the rich.
income segmentation affects income mobility in the Philippines, but not as much as one might think
The main takeaway from our work is that
income segmentation is an important factor that needs to be taken into consideration when studying income mobility in developing economies.
, in the context of the Philippines, income segmentation based on initial income may not be the best indicator of a household's future income prospects.
if we are interested in understanding the dynamics of inequality, we must consider the effects of income segmentation.
